hero.title: Phnom Penh Night Market
hero.subtitle: Set along the Tonle Sap riverfront, the Phnom Penh Night Market is a lively evening gathering place where locals and visitors browse stalls, enjoy street food, and experience the city's nightlife.

quickFacts.title: Quick Facts
quickFacts.intro: The essentials at a glance before you plan your visit.
quickFacts.note: The market is closed Monday – Thursday. It is an evening event, so stalls only start to open from around 5 PM.

intro.title: About Phnom Penh Night Market
body: The Phnom Penh Night Market (Khmer: ផ្សាររាត្រី ភ្នំពេញ) is an open-air evening market located on the riverfront along Preah Sisowath Quay, near the junction with Street 106 in central Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

On Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, as the sun sets, vendors set up stalls selling clothing, accessories, handicrafts, and souvenirs, while a large food section offers grilled dishes, noodles, and drinks beside the river.
More than a shopping spot, the market reflects everyday urban life in Cambodia's capital — a relaxed place where residents wind down and visitors get a feel for local culture after dark.

culture.title: History & Culture
body: Night markets are a long-standing part of urban life across Cambodia and Southeast Asia. Phnom Penh's riverside night market grew as the city's waterfront — near the confluence of the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers — became a focal point for public life after sunset, where cool river breezes have drawn residents to gather at dusk for generations.

Its signature is the open-air 'mat dining' tradition: the central plaza is laid with woven reed mats, and locals buy food from the stalls, slip off their shoes, and sit cross-legged with family and friends to share a meal — a living echo of rural Khmer communal feasting unique among Southeast Asian night markets.
Far from a tourist-only spectacle, Phsar Reatrey (ផ្សាររាត្រី ភ្នំពេញ) is where everyday Khmer life, handicraft heritage, and the modern city rhythm meet beside the water.

glossary.intro: A quick key to the local names you'll see around the market.

shopping.title: Shopping Experience
shopping.intro: Stroll through rows of stalls offering a mix of local and regional goods — look for these quintessential Khmer symbols.

items.title: Krama (ក្រមា)
items.desc: The iconic checkered cotton scarf with centuries of history — worn as a scarf, sun-shade, or all-purpose utility cloth in daily Khmer life.

items.title: Silver & Woodcarving
items.desc: Handmade silver jewelry and miniature red-ebony carvings inspired by Angkorian sculpture.

items.title: Silk & Textiles
items.desc: Handwoven scarves and silk products from Khmer weavers.

items.title: Souvenirs
items.desc: Postcards, magnets, and small keepsakes to remember your trip.

notes.stalls: Stalls are grouped roughly by type — clothing and accessories, handicrafts and silver, and souvenirs and gifts, with a dedicated street-food zone along the river.
notes.bargain: Haggling is normal and welcome at the market — keep it friendly. Most stalls take cash (USD or KHR); small purchases are easiest in riel or $1/$5 notes. Larger shops may accept card, ABA Pay or QR-code payment, but never assume it — carry some cash.

food.title: Top Street Food to Try at Phnom Penh Night Market
food.intro: The food court near the riverbank serves the most authentic Khmer home flavors — here are the dishes worth seeking out by name.

items.title: Sach Ko Yak (សាច់គោយ៉ាក់)
items.desc: Herbal grilled beef skewers marinated in lemongrass, turmeric, and kaffir lime leaf, charred over charcoal for a distinctly Southeast Asian aroma.

items.title: Lort Cha (ឆាចាប់)
items.desc: Short silver-pin noodles flash-fried with bean sprouts, chives, and egg, finished with a sweet-chili sauce — a favorite late-night energy boost.

items.title: Num Banh Chok (នំបញ្ចុក)
items.desc: Cambodia's national rice-noodle dish in a fragrant fish-curry broth, topped with fresh herbs and banana blossom.

items.title: Kuy Teav (គុយទាវ)
items.desc: Clear pork-bone broth simmered for hours, served with thin rice noodles, herbs, and beef or seafood.

items.title: Sugarcane & Kumquat Juice
items.desc: Fresh-pressed sugarcane juice with a squeeze of kumquat — sweet with a tangy lift, the classic way to cool off.

items.title: Around 17:00
items.desc: Stalls begin to open and the temperature eases after the afternoon heat.
Best atmosphere with full lighting, more vendors, and lively crowds.

items.title: Avoid Midday
items.desc: The market is an evening event; visiting at noon means little is open.

transport.title: How to Get to Riverside Night Market
transport.intro: The market sits on the central riverfront along Preah Sisowath Quay, within reach of most downtown areas.

modes.title: On Foot
modes.desc: Easy to reach on foot if you are staying near Sisowath Quay or the riverside.

modes.title: Tuk Tuk
modes.desc: A common, flexible way to get around Phnom Penh; agree on the fare first.

modes.title: Taxi / App
modes.desc: Ride-hailing apps operate in the city for a more comfortable trip.

modes.title: Public Transport
modes.desc: Local buses serve central Phnom Penh, though routes are limited at night.

modes.title: From the Airport
modes.desc: Phnom Penh International Airport (PNH) is about 10 km west of the city. A taxi or ride-hailing app (Grab/PassApp) takes roughly 30–45 minutes and costs around US$12–15 to Sisowath Quay; book at the official airport taxi counter or via the app. Tuk-tuks are cheaper but slower. From your drop-off, the market is a short walk along the riverside.

items.title: Sisowath Quay Riverside
items.desc: A riverside promenade for evening walks, city views, and open-air dining along the Tonle Sap.

items.title: Royal Palace Area
items.desc: Cambodia's royal compound and nearby temples showcase classic Khmer architecture.

items.title: Central Phnom Penh
items.desc: Explore the city center, including markets and streets close to the riverfront.

items.title: Remove Your Shoes
items.desc: Before stepping onto the central reed mats to eat, take off your shoes and leave them at the mat's edge — a basic sign of respect for local custom.

items.title: Cash & Currency
items.desc: Both USD and KHR are accepted. For small purchases use riel or small bills ($1/$5); change is often given in riel.

items.title: Stay Safe
items.desc: Along Sisowath Quay, keep phones and bags secure while photographing — occasional snatch theft occurs near the riverside.

items.title: Bargain Politely
items.desc: Haggling is normal at markets — keep it friendly and good-natured.

items.q: What are the opening hours of Phnom Penh Night Market?
items.a: The night market is open every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 5:00 PM to 11:00 PM. It is closed from Monday to Thursday.

items.q: Which days is Phnom Penh Night Market open?
items.a: It opens on weekends only — Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Plan your visit around those days, as the site is empty on other evenings.

items.q: Is there an entrance fee for the night market?
items.a: No, admission to the Phnom Penh Night Market is free. You only pay for the food and goods you buy.

items.q: What can visitors buy at the night market?
items.a: Visitors can find souvenirs, clothing, handicrafts, and a range of local goods.

items.q: Is the night market suitable for tourists?
items.a: Yes, it is a relaxed, family-friendly place to experience Phnom Penh's nightlife and market culture.

facilities.title: Visitor Facilities & Services
facilities.subtitle: To help you plan your trip, here is a practical overview of infrastructure and services around the night market and its surrounding area.
facilities.disclaimer: Note: As a non-profit guide, we list only categories of nearby facilities and do not recommend specific businesses.

items.title: Restrooms (WC)
points: Inside the market: paid public toilets are available within the market area, usually for a small maintenance fee (about 1,000 KHR / US$0.25). Carry some small change and tissue.
Nearby: the public promenade along the riverfront and adjacent commercial buildings also offer restroom facilities.

items.title: Parking & Transit
points: Motorbikes / e-bikes: designated temporary parking zones near the 106th & 108th Street entrances, managed by on-site staff for a small fee.
Cars: street parking along Preah Sisowath Quay is scarce at night due to crowds. Ride-hailing or tuk-tuk is recommended; if driving, use paid lots at nearby commercial buildings or hotels.
Tuk-tuk / ride-hailing: a drop-off and pick-up zone sits at the market main gate where it meets the riverside road, for quick stop-and-go.

items.title: ATMs & Currency Exchange
points: ATMs: several banks operate 24-hour ATMs around the market and along Sisowath Quay, supporting international cards (USD / KHR).
Currency exchange: licensed exchange points along the riverside let you convert foreign currency into small US dollars or Cambodian riel (KHR).

items.title: Dining Options
points: Market food court: central and riverside stalls offer charcoal grill, Khmer fried noodles, fresh spring rolls and fruit drinks, with the signature reed-mat picnic experience.
Riverside restaurants: indoor and open-air restaurants along Preah Sisowath Quay serve Khmer cuisine, French bistros, Asian fusion and Italian.
Rooftop bars: several high-rise buildings nearby have viewing bars overlooking the Tonle Sap river and Phnom Penh skyline.

items.title: Accommodation Categories
points: River-view boutique hotels: along Sisowath Quay, within walking distance of the market, ideal for the river sunset and night view.
Budget & backpacker hostels: behind the market (around 108th, 110th and 118th Streets), affordable for independent and young travellers.
Star-rated & business hotels: 10–15 minutes’ walk (near the Royal Palace or city main roads), full facilities for families and business trips.

items.title: Supermarkets & Retail
points: 24-hour convenience stores: several around the market and the riverside main road for water, mosquito repellent, snacks and daily needs.
Compact supermarkets: a few within walking distance offer imported food, household goods and personal care products.

items.title: Gas & EV Charging
points: Gas stations: the riverside market area is a scenic, pedestrian-dense zone; car fuel stations are mainly 5–10 minutes’ drive on city main roads (e.g. Preah Norodom Blvd or Preah Monivong Blvd).

EV charging: public charging in Phnom Penh is concentrated in large commercial complexes, upscale offices and some international-brand hotel parking lots. EV drivers should check open stations in advance via a maps app.

tips.title: Sockets & Voltage
tips.desc: Cambodia uses 220V. Common plugs are two-flat-pin (Type A) or two-round-pin (Type C).

tips.title: Payment
tips.desc: Market stalls mostly take cash (USD or KHR); larger supermarkets and restaurants nearby accept cards or QR payment.
